name: What is Puppet?
description:
Puppet is a configuration management system that allows you to define the state of your IT infrastructure, then automatically enforces the correct state.
It allows you to automate the installation and configuration of softwares across multiple systems regardless its operating system.You can run Puppet on all major Linux and Unix platforms, Mac OS X, and Windows.
Do you know who founded Puppet?
answer: Puppet is produced by Puppet Labs, founded by Luke Kanies in 2005.

name: How Puppet works?
description:
Puppet follows Client-Server model. The server (aka Master) communicates with client (aka Agent)over secure SSL connection.

Master system contains all configuration(manifests) files for different hosts.
Every 30 minutes, Agent will check with Master for configuration files and download the files in a form of catalog and applies them. Then Agent sends the status back to Master.

A catalog is a document that describes the desired system state for one specific computer. It lists all of the resources that need to be managed, as well as any dependencies between those resources.

Note:
We will use single node setup for quick start. Ideally, Puppet master and agent will be in separate nodes, agents can download configuration files only after Master accepts SSL certificate request from Client.

name: Install Puppet master and agent
description:
Lets add puppet yum repo and install it.
rpm -ivh http://yum.puppetlabs.com/puppetlabs-release-el-6.noarch.rpm
yum install -y puppet-server

Now we are ready to start the Puppet Master
/etc/init.d/puppetmaster start
and Puppet Agent
/etc/init.d/puppet start
If you want, you can check the version like:
puppet --version

Puppet can run in a stand-alone architecture, where each managed server has its own complete copy of your configuration info and compiles its own catalog. All configurations are stored in files under /etc/puppet/manifests/ These files ends with .pp extension.

name: Manage User resource
description:
Lets look at simple config file to create user resource webminal_user

cat > users.pp 
     user { 'webminal_user' :
             ensure => present,
           }

## Press ctrl+d to exit
Every 30 minutes, Puppet will make sure there exists a user named 'webminal_user'. Now we have a minimal setup which can be enforced on the machine. We can run puppet in simulation mode which doesn't perform any operation,

puppet apply users.pp --noop
Notice: /Stage[main]/Main/User[webminal_user]/ensure: current_value absent, should be present (noop)

Look above, it tells use current_value absent, we don't that user account and it should be present. Okay lets go ahead and run Puppet in local apply only mode

puppet apply users.pp
Notice: /Stage[main]/Main/User[webminal_user]/ensure: created
Nice :) Now it informs user is created.

Try running again, will won't display above 'created' message because we already have that user. So Puppet determines current state of resources within the system and compares with the configuration file - how we want the end system state to look like - If they don't match they it will apply and fix them.
We can view user resource details using puppet as

puppet resource user webminal_user

name: Manage File resource
description:
We have seen about user resource, now lets have a look at puppet file resource.
cat > rootfile.pp 
file { "/root/file.txt":
    ensure => "file",
    owner  => "root",
    group  => "wheel",
    mode   => 700,
}
We want to ensure there exists a file /root/file.txt with permission 700 for root user with group 'wheel'

puppet apply rootfile.pp
Notice: /Stage[main]/Main/File[/root/file.txt]/ensure: created Notice: Finished catalog run in 0.04 seconds
ls -l /root/file.txt
-rwx------. 1 root wheel 0 Sep 18 05:43 /root/file.txt
Lets assume some attacker changed its permission to 777. Please wear a mask before running below command :P
chmod 777 /root/file.txt
ls -l /root/file.txt
-rwxrwxrwx. 1 root wheel 0 Sep 18 05:43 /root/file.txt
Puppet can easily detect this mismatch and fix it when we run
puppet apply rootfile.pp
Notice: /Stage[main]/Main/File[/root/file.txt]/mode: mode changed '0777' to '0700' Notice: Finished catalog run in 0.04 seconds
Lets verify this
ls -l /root/file.txt
-rwx------. 1 root wheel 0 Sep 18 05:43 /root/file.txt

Cool!It regains its original state!
That's very high level basics of Puppet,it provides lot of other features. Please feel free to mess around with Puppet manifests. We will see more in upcoming sessions.
